newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Moody's confirms ratings for Australia's Telstra.
newsitem.headline: Moody's confirms ratings for Australia's Telstra.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it had confirmed Telstra Corp Ltd's Aa2 long-term and Prime-1 short term debt ratings.

Moody's said the confirmation was in response to Telstra's announcement that it intended to pay its owner, the Australian government, a special dividend of A$3 billion prior to its proposed partial privatisation.

"Telstra's use of debt to fund the special dividend will result in the company exhausting most of its financial flexibility within its rating category, but its debt protection measurements remain in line with its rating peers," it said.

Moody's said the confirmation reflected the company's leading position within the Australian telecommunications market, the government's continued retention of 70 percent of Telstra's equity after the proposed partial privatisation and the company's strong operating margin and stable cash flow.

Moody's said Telstra's operating margin and cash flow would face downward pressure due to more of its markets experiencing increased competition as the Australian telecommunications market becomes further deregulated after July.

"Telstra's management will be challenged to meet its revenue and cost cutting initiatives to maintain its strong operating margin and cash flow in the increasingly competitive market - any slippage could result in Telstra's debt protection deteriorating, thereby placing pressure upon its rating," the ratings agency said.

Moody's said Telstra's debt protection measurements would deteriorate as a result of the use of debt to fund the special dividend. It said leverage was expected to peak at about 45 percent while interest coverage was likely to deteriorate to about five times as a result of the increased interest burden.

"The increase in debt service requirements and the company's substantial capital expenditure programme necessary to modernise its network will challenge management to maintain appropriate gearing levels," Moody's said. The confirmation also applies to paper issued by Australian and Overseas Telecommunications.
